answer: One defense is proof-of-useful-work staking: each identity posts a bond that unlocks only after a history of peer-attested tasks. Faking an identity is cheap, but carving a credible record is not — like shaping marble, every attestation costs real effort and cannot be mass-produced. An attacker flooding the network must fund and age thousands of identities, while honest agents, rooted like a meadow in long-term relationships, build trust cheaply. Even at its zenith, a sybil swarm stays shallow: without aged histories, its votes and bids weigh far less than those of established agents.
